sections.title: If you write long, a strategy for distribution

items.label: The 2% stat
items.copy:
a16z published State of Markets II, 100+ charts on the first half of 2026.

One stood out: as of April, only about 2% of US households were paying for an AI subscription.

If you're reading this, you're likely in that 2%, and it's easy to forget how small that is.

items.label: Hook: the unposted backlog
items.copy:
On October 1 the dashboard read 144 sections across my last 8 issues. 35 had been posted. 109 never had.

That's 76% of my work that only ever lived inside a newsletter.

SHORTCUTS is mostly tools and methods that keep, so issues #01 through #06 are a stockpile.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: The method in one line
items.copy:
Write for yourself, at length. Then let a tool find the hooks, break the piece down by platform, and hand you a plan and a checklist you can see.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: 4-post thread: X's small-account boost
items.copy:
1/ On September 30, X changed its ranking code to lift smaller accounts.

2/ Under 50,000 followers, one eligible new post per feed load can be placed near the top of some feeds, but only in its first two hours and until it passes about 200 views.

3/ Early reactions decide how far it goes from there, and X's ranking code weights a reply ten times a like.

4/ So answer replies for those two hours.

items.label: The dashboard
items.copy: I'm a visual person, this changed my behavior. The dashboard shows every issue, section, and where each has been posted, with a tick and a link for logging. At a glance I can see my progress across each issue.

items.label: Hook: 15 of 394 rules
items.copy:
Of 394 rules, about 15 reached a session at startup.

I found out the hard way, most of my rules never reached the agent at all.

Claude caps what a hook can load at 10,000 characters; past that, the model gets a 2,000-character preview and a file path, the rest sits unread.

If you load anything into an agent at the start (a rules file, a project brief, a style guide), keep what a hook prints under 10,000 characters and put the rest somewhere the agent can search.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: Green lights on broken work
items.copy:
In one week I found four monitors saying everything was fine when it wasn't.

A check that only confirms a job ran is not a check. Make it confirm the job delivered.

items.label: The honest wait
items.copy: Fixing delivery took a day. By next quarter I'll know the impact.

items.label: Hook: what passed, what failed
items.copy:
Jev is a decision model, not a writer.

I tested it on my own work over the past two weeks. One kind of task passed and three failed.

Why it failed: the information it needed can't be written. Taste lives in my head. Judgment needs context from elsewhere. A sorter can't go get it.

Eligibility lives in the listing and runs at volume, so it worked.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: What it is
items.copy:
Jev is a decision model, not a writer.

It hands back the answer and a confidence number.

Each decision costs a fraction of a cent and usually takes under a second.

items.label: Hook: agentic buying
items.copy:
Instinct is a personal assistant you text or call.

40% of users handed it a credit card within three weeks, Shinn said on Patrick O'Shaughnessy's podcast.

When agents hold your card, can access your accounts and know your preferences to decide where you buy, it opens a whole new arms race for customer acquisition.

If you sell, your next customer may be an agent reading your page: price, stock, shipping and returns it can understand, or it moves on.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: The terms
items.copy:
From this week's SHORTCUTS:

The terms put the risk on you. What Instinct agrees to for you is "binding on you as if entered into directly by you," so a nonrefundable booking it makes counts as one you made.
